title: The fundamental rule cannot be found by working backwards from known laws

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The fundamental rule cannot be found by working backwards from known laws

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If the ultimate rule for the universe is simple, it cannot realistically be found by engineering it from observed features; the only practical method is to choose a straightforward representation and systematically search through large numbers of candidate rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: my guess is that the only realistic way to find the rule in the first place will be to start from some very straightforward representation, and then just to search through large numbers of possible rules in this representation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Ultimate Models for the Universe” (from p. 465), p. 468. Scope: methodology for finding a fundamental theory of physics

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-09: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.16

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Historical and computational case studies could compare selected discovery methods, but they cannot decide the exclusive claim as stated. Its conclusion depends on future discovery and subjective notions of realism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No finite comparison of theory-discovery strategies can establish that systematic search is the only realistic route to an unknown fundamental rule, because success, representation, and realism are unspecified and the target rule is unknown.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Counterfactual methodological claim.

Success and practicality lack fixed criteria.

The true fundamental rule and search representation are unknown.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a judgment about methodology: working backwards from known laws will not realistically yield a simple ultimate rule, and blind search is the only practical route. No public dataset records attempts against a known target, and either success or failure of a strategy can be redescribed to fit the claim. It has no measurable consequence that would settle it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: There is no decision criterion that separates 'the only realistic method' from rival search strategies, because the target ultimate rule is not an identified object with a recorded discovery path.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The target rule is unknown, so there is no outcome that counts as finding it.

Failure of inverse engineering does not show that it cannot work, and a successful search would not show it was the only practical method.
